issues.legal_issue: A suit to recover a hereditary shebaitship is governed by the limitation rule for hereditary offices rather than the rule for recovery of immovable property after the death of a female holder.
material_facts: The disputed interest was a share of a hereditary shebaitship, held in turns of worship.
A widow succeeded to the shebaitship after her husband’s death, and the claimants sought the interest as the next heirs of the last male holder after the widow died.
issues.conclusion: The suit was governed by Article 124, not Article 141, of the Limitation Act. Shebaitship is a hereditary office of peculiar character and does not fall within the category of immovable property covered by Article 141.
issues.legal_principle: Article 141 applies to suits concerning immovable property, whereas Article 124 expressly covers hereditary offices. Shebaitship combines elements of office and property, but its peculiar and anomalous character does not make it immovable property in the legal sense. Because the shebaiti interest is hereditary and follows the line of inheritance from the founder, a female successor has a widow’s limited interest in it; that does not change the classification of the right for limitation purposes. The Court did not accept the reasoning in Pydigantan v. Rama Dass and Lilabati v. Bishen insofar as it treated the female shebait’s rights as unqualified, and relied on the established character of shebaitship as both office and property, including Angurbala v. Debabrata.

predicates.suit_to_recover_shebaitship: The claimant brought a suit seeking recovery of a shebaitship interest.
predicates.claim_concerns_hereditary_office: The disputed right passes by inheritance as a hereditary office.
predicates.shebaitship_is_not_ordinary_immovable_pr: The disputed shebaitship has the peculiar character of an office and property, rather than being ordinary immovable property.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks recovery of a shebaitship that passes as a hereditary office and is not ordinary immovable property, the hereditary-office limitation rule applies.

issues.legal_issue: Adverse possession against a female holder of a limited interest does not start limitation against a reversioner who claims from the last male holder rather than through that female holder.
material_facts: The widow held the shebaitship interest as the limited successor to her husband.
A transferee took possession under an alienation by the widow, and that possession was adverse to her.
The claimants sought the interest as heirs of the last male holder, not through the widow, and sued after her death.
issues.conclusion: The adverse possession against the widow did not bar the claimants. For their claim, limitation began when succession opened to them on the widow’s death, so the suit was not time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 124, read with section 2(8) of the Limitation Act, the defendant’s possession must be adverse to the plaintiff or to someone from or through whom the plaintiff derives the right to sue. A reversioner does not derive title through the widow but claims from the last male holder; accordingly, adverse possession against the widow does not begin limitation against the reversioner before succession opens. The principle that adverse possession against a Hindu widow does not defeat the reversioner is not confined to Article 141. The Court relied on Gnanasambanda v. Velu for the requirement that possession be adverse to the plaintiff or the person through whom the plaintiff claims, and affirmed the principle recognized in Srinath Kuer v. Prosunno Kumar, Banchordas v. Parvati, and Jaggo v. Utsava.

rule.if: suit_to_recover_hereditary_office and female_holder_has_limited_interest and claimant_succeeds_from_last_male_holder and possession_is_adverse_to_female_holder

predicates.suit_to_recover_hereditary_office: The claimant brought a suit to recover a hereditary office.
predicates.female_holder_has_limited_interest: A female holder possessed the interest as a limited successor to the prior male holder.
predicates.claimant_succeeds_from_last_male_holder: The claimant’s title arises from the last male holder rather than through the female holder.
predicates.possession_is_adverse_to_female_holder: The defendant or a predecessor possessed the interest adversely to the female holder.

issues.definition: If possession is adverse to a limited female holder but the claimant succeeds from the last male holder, limitation for the claimant begins when succession opens to the claimant.
